requiredFindings.title: Validate every gitlink element before comparing paths
requiredFindings.problem: The per-element loop compares a validated g against every other h before validating those other elements. With memberGitlinks={"/h/w/a": ["sub", 17]} on an otherwise valid conventional candidate, discover raises TypeError (unsupported operand types for +: int and str) from _within, rather than ValueError("MEMBER_GITLINKS_INCONSISTENT:/h/w/a"). Reversing the same invalid entries to [17, "sub"] produces the documented rejection. Thus malformed-table rejection depends on element order, and the new validator does not implement its stated closed inconsistency contract. A non-mapping table also reaches .items without a shape check. These inputs fail closed; this finding does not claim a traversal bypass.
requiredFindings.requiredChange: Validate the table/container shape and all element types and individual canonical paths before duplicate/prefix comparisons. Then check relationships only among validated strings. Preserve the documented MEMBER_GITLINKS_INCONSISTENT rejection for invalid keyed lists, and explicitly define the rejection for an invalid table container rather than exposing incidental Python exceptions.
requiredFindings.validation: Add invalid-element controls with a non-string before and after a valid string, plus non-list values and a non-mapping table. Assert the intended exception type and diagnostic, independent of element order, before discovery or item-6b consultation. Refresh the checker, evidence and exact pins.

nonBlockingObservations.title: No-member equality is regression coverage, not a universal equivalence proof
nonBlockingObservations.observation: All 64 existing discovery cases remain equal, but global grammar priority intentionally changes some inputs even when no member is ultimately admitted, for example ["missing", "../bad"]. The new D15 cases bind that documented change. The 64-case result is valid as stated; it must not be generalized to all no-member inputs or to every behavior outside a supplied member set.
